title: UPPER PUSH AND POSTURE
subtitle: TUESDAY UPPER BODY. SEATED FIRST, THEN STANDING AT THE WALL AND CHAIR. NO FLOOR TODAY. KIND HIPS.

script.welcome: Good morning Pam. I'm Stratton. Tuesday is upper push and posture, about ten minutes. We start in the chair with a posture row, a gentle overhead press, and a light figure four for the hips, then we stand for wall push ups and a kind hip flexor stretch at the chair. No floor today. Hand weights are optional, and empty hands are perfectly fine. A smaller range is fine on sore-joint days. Well done for showing up.
script.start: Whenever you're ready. Sit tall near the front of a sturdy chair, feet flat, shoulders soft, slow easy breath.
script.nextExercise: Next one. Settle in. No rush at all.
script.lastSet: Last one of these. Keep it comfortable.
script.complete: That's us, Pam. Shoulders open, posture tall, hips looked after. A lovely little break from the desk. Have a sip of water and enjoy your Tuesday. Well done.
script.pause: Paused. Take all the time you need.
script.resume: Back with you. Easy as we go.

exercises.name: SEATED POSTURE ROW
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of the chair, feet flat. Hold light hand weights or nothing at all, arms reaching forward at chest height, palms facing each other. Draw the elbows back alongside the ribs and gently squeeze the shoulder blades together, chest proud, then reach forward again slowly. Keep the shoulders down away from the ears. Empty hands are perfectly fine. Stop if anything in the shoulders or neck feels sharp.
exercises.speakStart: Seated posture row. Two rounds of eight. Sit tall, reach forward, then draw the elbows back and squeeze the shoulder blades together. Empty hands are fine.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Arms down. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Rows done. Lovely tall posture already.

exercises.name: SEATED GENTLE OVERHEAD PRESS
exercises.cue: Sit tall with your back away from the chair, feet flat, tummy gently in. Start with hands at shoulder height, elbows a little forward, holding light weights or nothing. Press up slowly, only as high as feels comfortable, then lower with control. Halfway up is plenty on sore-shoulder days. No arching the low back. Stop if you feel sharp shoulder or neck pain.
exercises.speakStart: Seated gentle overhead press. Two rounds of six. Hands at shoulder height, press up slowly, only as high as is comfortable, and lower with control. Halfway is plenty on a sore day.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty seconds. Hands in your lap. Shoulders soft.
exercises.speakDone: Press done. Strong, steady work, Pam.

exercises.name: SEATED FIGURE-FOUR (LIGHT)
exercises.cue: Sit tall near the front of the chair, feet flat. Rest the right ankle over the left thigh, just above the knee. Stay tall and tip forward from the hips only a touch, until you feel a mild stretch in the outer hip or buttock. Hold about twenty seconds, then switch sides. Keep it light: never press the knee down or fold deep. If the left groin or front of the hip pinches on that side, skip it or simply rest the ankle without leaning. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness. When you're done, stand up and come to the wall.
exercises.speakStart: Seated figure four, nice and light. About twenty seconds each side. Rest one ankle over the other thigh, sit tall, and tip forward just a touch. Never forced.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Both feet down. Then stand up nice and easy and come to the wall.
exercises.speakDone: Figure four done. Hips looked after. Up we come, nice and steady, and over to the wall.

exercises.name: WALL PUSH-UPS
exercises.cue: Stand facing the wall, about an arm's length away, feet hip-width. Place your hands on the wall at shoulder height, a little wider than the shoulders. Keep the body in one long line, then bend the elbows to bring the chest toward the wall, and press back out slowly. Step closer to the wall to make it easier; a small bend is plenty on sore-wrist or sore-shoulder days. Stop if anything feels sharp.
exercises.speakStart: Wall push ups. Two rounds of six. Hands on the wall at shoulder height, body long, bend the elbows and press back out slowly. Step closer to make it easier.
exercises.speakRest: Twenty five seconds. Hands down. Shake the arms out.
exercises.speakDone: Wall push ups done. That's real upper body strength, Pam. Now come to the chair back.

exercises.name: STANDING HIP FLEXOR
exercises.cue: Stand beside the chair with one hand lightly on the chair back. Step one foot back about half a step, not a deep lunge, both feet pointing forward, knees soft. Gently tuck the pelvis under, belt buckle toward the ribs, until you feel a mild stretch at the front of the back hip. A tiny lean is enough. Let the free arm float up gently for a touch of posture. Breathe slowly for about twenty seconds, then swap legs. Start with the left leg back and keep that side extra gentle. Stop if you feel sharp groin pain, spreading pain, numbness, tingling, or weakness.
exercises.speakStart: Standing hip flexor to finish. About twenty seconds each leg, twice through. Hand on the chair, small step back, tuck the pelvis, tiny lean. Left leg first, extra gentle.
exercises.speakRest: Fifteen seconds. Feet together. Easy breath.
exercises.speakDone: Hip flexor stretch done. That's the session, Pam. Upper body and posture all looked after. Have a grand Tuesday.
